data.title: A1: What made up the 2007–11 jump?
data.markdown:
# A1: What made up the 2007–11 jump?

> **Claude draft, not the author's text.** Evidence and a proposed reading for Eleonora's own write-up. Every number has a register row; 3 of the 26 (the 2007Q4 and 2011Q4 shares and the 13.1 pp jump) have passed a validation check, and the other 23 are unverified (recomputed by the skeptic, no automated check yet); the wording, framing and conclusions are hers to write.

**PLAN task A1. Status: analysis done; method decided by Eleonora (Shapley, 2026-11-04); the write-up is a Claude draft for her to replace.** The skeptic and quant-reviewer agents reviewed it (`claims/review-log.md`, R-20261104-1 to -12). Data: Fed Z.1, `Z1.csv` dated 2026-09-11. Every number here has a row in [`claims/register.csv`](../../claims/register.csv), and every policy date is checked against a primary source ([`sources.md`](sources.md)).

## Result

From 2007Q4 to 2011Q4 the public share of household mortgages and consumer credit rose from 36.1% to 49.2%, +13.1 pp (validation check C5). A little over half of that came from private holdings shrinking: private retreat explains 6.9 pp and public growth 6.2 pp. The parts add up to the total exactly.

**Method.** Shapley, per Eleonora's decision of 2026-11-04: the public side's contribution is the average of counting it first and counting it last, and the private side gets the rest. Within each side, each holder's share is proportional to its change in holdings. The endpoint-weighted identity of the first draft gave public 7.1 pp and private 6.0 pp, which reverses the order; the quarter-by-quarter Shapley path matches the Shapley endpoints to one decimal. All three are in `results.json` (`sensitivity`).

**Which public holders grew:**

| Component | Change in holdings | Contribution |
|---|---|---|
| Ginnie Mae pools (FHA, VA, USDA loans) | +$746B | 3.3 pp |
| Federal student loans | +$379B | 1.7 pp |
| Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac (portfolio + pools) | +$278B | 1.2 pp |

All other public holders combined (FHLBs, other GSEs, federal direct mortgages, state and local) were net zero to one decimal.

**Which private holders shrank.** Private-label securitization and mortgage REITs held $1.71T less, which contributed 5.7 pp. Part of that is accounting: FAS 166/167 moved securitized loans, mostly card ABS, onto bank balance sheets in 2010Q1 (`path.csv`), which leaves the private total unchanged. Banks, credit unions and other private holders contributed the rest of the 6.9 pp.

**Own-share view.** Measured by each public holder's own share of the total, which spreads the private retreat across them: Ginnie pools +6.1 pp, Fannie and Freddie +3.9 pp, federal student loans +3.1 pp. Summed into the catalog's buckets, this reproduces `analysis/results.json` `gfc_window_split_pp` exactly. It describes composition and says nothing about cause.

**What this changes.**
- **The largest public increase was in Ginnie Mae pools (FHA/VA/USDA loans).** Fannie and Freddie grew less but still held far more: $4.34T against Ginnie pools' $1.13T in 2011Q4. VA and USDA guarantees are partial, and FHA loans held by banks, or bought out of Ginnie pools, count as private here.
- **Fannie and Freddie's piece came early and partly reversed.** Per `path.csv`, they had contributed 1.1 pp by 2008Q2, the last quarter-end before the September 2008 conservatorship, peaked at 2.3 pp in 2009Q4 and fell back afterwards. Their balances grew $278B over the window.
- **These data cannot test whether the conservatorship ratcheted risk onto the public.** The GSEs count as public at every date, so the conservatorship changes nothing in this accounting. Whether it changed how much the GSEs held, or what their debt cost, is a counterfactual question for A7.

## Dated policy events

The decomposition is an accounting; the causal estimate is A7. Events are matched to components by topic: federal student loans, for example, had moved only 0.03 pp by 2008Q2 and grew most after mid-2010. Each date and citation was checked on 2026-11-04 against the official text (GovInfo for statutes, FHFA, the Fed's Z.1 release); URLs, file hashes and quoted sections are in [`sources.md`](sources.md).

| Date | Event | Component it lines up with |
|---|---|---|
| 13 Feb 2008 | Economic Stimulus Act of 2008 (P.L. 110-185), Secs. 201–202: temporary rise in GSE and FHA loan limits | Ginnie pools; Fannie and Freddie |
| 7 May 2008 | Ensuring Continued Access to Student Loans Act (P.L. 110-227), Sec. 7: temporary authority to buy FFEL loans | Federal student loans |
| 30 Jul 2008 | Housing and Economic Recovery Act (P.L. 110-289), Secs. 1101 and 1117: creates FHFA; temporary Treasury authority to buy GSE obligations | Fannie and Freddie |
| 6–7 Sep 2008 | FHFA places Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac in conservatorship (6 Sep); Treasury preferred-stock agreements signed (7 Sep) | Fannie and Freddie |
| 17 Feb 2009 | American Recovery and Reinvestment Act (P.L. 111-5), Secs. 1202–1203: FHA and GSE loan limits for 2009 | Ginnie pools; Fannie and Freddie |
| 2010Q1 | FAS 166 and 167: Z.1 moves consolidated securitizations from the pool and ABS sectors onto GSE, bank and finance-company balance sheets, "almost all" in 2010Q1 (Fed Z.1 release, 10 Jun 2010) | Accounting only (see limits) |
| 30 Mar 2010 | Health Care and Education Reconciliation Act (P.L. 111-152), Sec. 2201 (SAFRA): no new FFEL loans first disbursed after 30 Jun 2010 | Federal student loans |

## Limits

- **Holding is not guaranteeing.** Most FFEL loans held by banks before 2010 already carried a federal guarantee, so the student-loan component overstates the shift in credit risk. FHA and VA loans held directly by banks are federally insured but count as private here. Net exposure is task A2.
- **FAS 166/167 reshuffled private holders in 2010Q1.** Card ABS moved onto bank balance sheets, so the private-label line jumps and the bank line falls in that quarter. The private side's contribution depends only on the private total, so these reclassifications cancel. The same consolidation moved GSE pool MBS from sector 41 to sector 40, which is why Fannie and Freddie are shown as portfolio plus pools.
- **Ginnie label.** The Ginnie line includes the small FmHA pool line (FL413065133), which is zero at both endpoints.
- **Apportioning.** Mortgage holders are scaled to the household liability, as in the rest of the project, assuming the same holder mix for household and business 1–4 family mortgages.
- **"Other GSEs" is partly a residual:** FL403065105 minus the Fannie, Freddie and FHLB lines. It is under $20B.
- **A different counterfactual gives different words.** `analysis/findings.md` says that had private debt stayed at its 2007Q4 level, the share would have risen 6.1 pp. That is the public-growth side of a split that holds private debt fixed; the Shapley split averages over both orders. Both say about half of the jump came from private retreat.
- **Pool sub-series before 1987.** In the 2026-09-11 vintage the four pool lines (FL413065110, FL413065123, FL413065133, FL413065143) exceed the pool total FL413065105 from 1974Q3 to 1986Q3, by up to $21.4B ($14.6B in 1980Q4). Inside A1's window they match exactly, and `decompose.py` asserts this every run. A1 should stay inside 1987 onwards with these cells until the gap is explained. The markets track found the gap on 2026-11-04.
- **Revisions.** The figures are from the 2026-09-11 vintage. Rerun after each Z.1 release.

## Files and how to rerun

```bash
uv run --project pipeline python validation/run.py        # downloads the Z.1 zip if absent
uv run --project pipeline python research/a1_gfc_decomposition/decompose.py
```

- `decompose.py`: the decomposition (Shapley; the endpoint identity as a sensitivity). It asserts that the parts sum to the total and that the cells reproduce the scope total.
- `test_decompose.py`: synthetic tests of both methods.
- `decomposition.csv`: endpoint contributions by loan type × holder (all holders).
- `own_share_change.csv`: the own-share view (public holders).
- `path.csv`: cumulative chained contributions by quarter, grouped.
- `results.json`: headline numbers for the register.
- `sources.md`: the primary sources for the policy dates, with hashes.
- Method decision: [`docs/decisions/a1-decomposition.md`](../../docs/decisions/a1-decomposition.md).

# Joint holdout results (C2 forecast, C1 and C1b nowcasts)

> **Claude draft.** Written by the markets track from the result files. Eleonora replaces it with her own text before anything here is published.

The holdout is 2023Q3–2026Q2. It was opened once, in commit a0d9151, under Eleonora's approval 432fed0 and after deviation c1b-dev-1 (cddd3ca). Source files: `research/c2_forecast/holdout_results.json`, `research/c1b_nowcast/holdout_results.json` and `research/c1b_nowcast/nowcasts_holdout.csv`. Every number below comes from those files through `make_readme_and_rows.py`; none was typed by hand.

Each cell rests on 12 targets or fewer, so these are small-sample numbers.

## C1b: does Freddie Mac's monthly data improve the real-time nowcast?

RMSE in percentage points of the public share, real-time first-release targets. k is the nowcast instant within the quarter.

| k | scored instants | C1b bridge | C1 bridge | no change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| k = 1 | 12 | 0.14 pp | 0.15 pp | 0.20 pp |
| k = 2 | 12 | 0.13 pp | 0.15 pp | 0.20 pp |
| k = 3 | 11 | 0.15 pp | 0.18 pp | 0.20 pp |
| pooled k = 1–3 | 35 | 0.14 pp | 0.16 pp | 0.20 pp |

Pre-registered verdict (`docs/decisions/c1b-prereg.md`, decision rules): **improves on C1**. The rule needs lower RMSE at every k on development, significant after Holm at one or more k, and a lower pooled RMSE in the holdout. The holdout part is a comparison of RMSEs, with no test.

## C1: the accounting bridge in real time

Bridge RMSE relative to no-change on the same instants. The holdout carries no tests.

| k | instants | bridge / no change |
|---|---|---|
| k = 1 | 12 | 0.75 |
| k = 2 | 12 | 0.76 |
| k = 3 | 11 | 0.92 |
| pooled k = 1–3 | 35 | 0.81 |

Mean bridge error over the holdout instants: −0.08 pp (negative: the bridge nowcast is below the outcome).

Targets scored: 12 quarters. The 2 instants that target 2026Q3 are recorded as "no target" (deviation c1b-dev-1): no Z.1 has published that quarter, and it lies outside the holdout window.

## C2: the share forecasts (h = 1, 4 and 8 quarters ahead) against their benchmarks

Holdout RMSE of the candidate divided by the benchmark's, with the pre-registered verdict (`docs/decisions/scoring-protocol.md`, option (a)): "beats" needs a lower loss on development, significant after Holm, and a lower loss in the holdout. "Does not beat" means the benchmark's loss is lower in either sample, so it can sit beside a holdout ratio below 1 when the development loss was higher. Pseudo out-of-sample on latest-vintage data, not real time.

| design | h | candidate | vs no change | vs AR (BIC) | vs seasonal naive |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| expanding | 1 | Z-DIR | 1.16 (does not beat) | 0.94 (comparable) | 0.87 (beats) |
| expanding | 1 | Z-DAMP | 1.10 (does not beat) | 0.89 (comparable) | 0.83 (beats) |
| expanding | 1 | ZC1-DIR | 1.31 (does not beat) | 1.07 (does not beat) | 0.99 (comparable) |
| expanding | 4 | Z-DIR | 1.40 (does not beat) | 0.97 (does not beat) | 0.83 (comparable) |
| expanding | 4 | Z-DAMP | 1.42 (does not beat) | 0.98 (comparable) | 0.84 (comparable) |
| expanding | 4 | ZC1-DIR | 3.98 (does not beat) | 2.77 (does not beat) | 2.36 (does not beat) |
| expanding | 8 | Z-DIR | 1.90 (does not beat) | 1.02 (does not beat) | 0.66 (comparable) |
| expanding | 8 | Z-DAMP | 1.31 (does not beat) | 0.70 (does not beat) | 0.45 (comparable) |
| rolling | 1 | Z-DIR | 1.16 (does not beat) | 0.90 (comparable) | 0.87 (comparable) |
| rolling | 1 | Z-DAMP | 1.09 (does not beat) | 0.85 (comparable) | 0.82 (beats) |
| rolling | 4 | Z-DIR | 1.34 (does not beat) | 0.84 (comparable) | 0.79 (does not beat) |
| rolling | 4 | Z-DAMP | 1.42 (does not beat) | 0.88 (comparable) | 0.84 (comparable) |
| rolling | 8 | Z-DIR | 2.15 (does not beat) | 1.21 (does not beat) | 0.74 (comparable) |
| rolling | 8 | Z-DAMP | 1.31 (does not beat) | 0.74 (comparable) | 0.45 (comparable) |

No candidate beats no-change at any horizon or design (0 "beats" verdicts against no-change). The 3 "beats" verdicts are all against the seasonal naive at h = 1. Coverage of the intervals and the full score tables are in the results file.

data.title: B4: Policy-regime scenarios
data.markdown:
# B4: Policy-regime scenarios

> **Claude draft, not the author's text.** The status of each policy debate was looked up from primary sources on 2026-11-04 ([`sources.md`](sources.md)). How each scenario maps onto the B3 engine is Eleonora's choice: the recession range follows her Q-B3 decision, the GSE range her card b4-gse (a). The student-loan scenario is left out for now (card b4-student-2 (iii)). Method: [`METHOD.md`](METHOD.md).

**PLAN task B4. Status: recession range and GSE-release range done; the student-loan scenario has a CBO budget-side proxy (card cbo-repo-55 (b)) and, beside it, ED's estimate of the fall in federal lending (docket 56 (b)), both 2026-11-11; no loss-engine change until Eleonora reviews them.**

| Scenario | Status of the debate (as looked up, 2026-11-04) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Recession | – | Losses from $595B to $1,886B on 2026Q2 balances. The public share of losses is 23% to 42% (federal student loans excluded: no loss rate in either preset). The range runs from B3's DFAST proxy to its 2008–12 replay; both are proxies. |
| GSEs released from conservatorship | FHFA's conservatorship page, retrieved 2026-11-04, says "Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac continue to operate under conservatorship, as they have since 2008". The page carries no date of its own and cites the 2025 Scorecard, so it may lag. Only the first page of FHFA news releases (10 items) was checked, and none concerned an exit. So the status is **unconfirmed beyond those two pages**. | Public share of mortgage and other consumer-credit losses (federal student loans excluded) from 7% to 42% across both recession proxies and 0–100% of the Fannie and Freddie book turning private (below). |
| Student-loan reform | P.L. 119-21, approved July 4, 2025: no Federal Direct PLUS loans for graduate and professional students for periods from July 1, 2026, subject to the statute's transition exception ("Subject to paragraph (8)"); new limits; a Repayment Assistance Plan. | Budget-side proxy only (Eleonora, card cbo-repo-55 (b), 2026-11-11; section below). CBO's projected outlays of the Direct Loan program account over FY2026–FY2035 fell from $189B in its January 2025 baseline to $35B in its February 2026 baseline. These outlays are what the account pays out for the cost of federal direct loans, not the amount lent, and the change is not a CBO estimate of the law's effect or of lending moving to private lenders. ED's final rule estimates that federal non-consolidated student-loan disbursements over 2026–2035 fall by $223.9B (volume side, section below). No public share changes. |

- **No transfer.** Neither range applies a CRT or mortgage-insurance transfer. With A2's cover as an input, the public figures would be lower.
- **Two kinds of bound.** The two recession ends differ in horizon as well as severity: nine quarters of stressed bank loss rates against five years of realized bank charge-offs. The upper end is probably an upper bound for the public book (`research/b3_scenarios/README.md`).

## GSE release: who bears the losses (card b4-gse (a))

**What moves.** On release, a share of the losses on Fannie Mae's and Freddie Mac's books (portfolio and pools) turns private: 0% (losses stay on the GSEs' and Treasury's side, as under conservatorship), then 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% (fully private, no backstop). These are scenario points and forecast nothing about release terms. Balances and loss rates stay as in B3; only the side of the losses changes.

**What stays public.** Ginnie Mae and FmHA pools, the FHLBs and the other GSEs. The Ginnie pools are federally insured or guaranteed loans (FHA, VA, USDA); VA and USDA guaranties are partial and issuers bear part of the loss, so counting the whole pool as public is a holder-based simplification (see A1's caveat). The split of B3's "GSEs & agency pools" mortgage book ($8,977B, household-apportioned, 2026Q2, from the 2026-09-11 Z.1 release):
- Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, the book that is released: $6,277B (Fannie $3,329B, Freddie $2,948B).
- Ginnie Mae and FmHA pools: $2,611B.
- FHLBs and other GSEs: $90B.

**Result.** Public losses and the public share of losses on mortgages and other consumer credit, by share of the Fannie/Freddie book's losses that turns private. Federal student loans are excluded: neither B3 preset gives them a loss rate, so they add no loss.

| Share turning private | DFAST 2026 proxy: public losses | Public share of losses | 2008–12 replay proxy: public losses | Public share of losses |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0% | $137B | 23% | $801B | 42% |
| 25% | $114B | 19% | $663B | 35% |
| 50% | $90B | 15% | $526B | 28% |
| 75% | $67B | 11% | $389B | 21% |
| 100% | $43B | 7% | $252B | 13% |

Total losses do not change with the share: $595B under the DFAST proxy and $1,886B under the replay. At 0% the figures equal the recession range above.

**Caveats.**
- **What "public" means here.** Losses on the books of the GSEs, the federal government and other public holders. Under conservatorship the GSEs' own capital takes losses first and Treasury's Senior Preferred Stock Purchase Agreements stand behind them, so "public" is wider than taxpayer outlay.
- **Gross of existing risk transfer.** The shares are measured before CRT and mortgage insurance. Fannie and Freddie already pass part of their losses to private investors and insurers today (A2, `research/a2_net_exposure/`), so on a net basis today's arrangement already sits above 0%.
- **One loss rate per class.** B3 applies one mortgage loss rate to every holder, so Fannie and Freddie lose at the same rate as Ginnie's FHA and VA pools. If Ginnie's pools lose more per dollar than the GSE book, the public share at each point is understated, and overstated if they lose less. Relative loss rates are not estimated here.
- **Proxies.** Both loss paths are bank-portfolio proxies (B3).
- **Release and loss-bearing differ.** A released GSE would hold more capital and could buy more CRT. The share turning private stands in for those terms, which are not known (option (c) of the card, a specific proposal, was not chosen).

## Student-loan reform: a CBO budget-side proxy (card cbo-repo-55 (b))

> **Claude draft.** Eleonora chose (2026-11-11) to add CBO's data repository as a source for budget-side context only, and to use the Direct Loan account's outlays as a labeled proxy here. Method: `METHOD.md` section 3b. Sources, commit and hashes: [`sources.md`](sources.md).

**What the number is.** CBO's baseline projections of spending by budget account, for the "Federal Direct Student Loan Program Account" (TIN 091-0243-0-1-502). Under the Federal Credit Reform Act, a credit program account receives "an appropriation to cover the cost" of the loans, where cost is their net present value to the government (2 U.S.C. 661a). Reestimates of that cost are shown in a subaccount of the same account, and administrative funding may be too (2 U.S.C. 661c). So these outlays are what this account pays out for the **cost** of federal direct loans. They are not the amount lent: loans are paid out through a financing account, which is not in CBO's file. They are not a complete net subsidy cost either: the sources fetched here do not establish where a negative subsidy is recorded.

**PROXY.** Projected outlays in the January 2025 baseline against the February 2026 baseline (the repository's file labels; P.L. 119-21 was approved between them, on July 4, 2025), FY2026–FY2035:

| Fiscal year | January 2025 baseline | February 2026 baseline |
|---|---|---|
| FY2026 | $16.7B | $3.9B |
| FY2027 | $17.6B | $3.7B |
| FY2028 | $18.1B | $3.1B |
| FY2029 | $18.4B | $2.8B |
| FY2030 | $18.8B | $3.0B |
| FY2031 | $19.1B | $3.3B |
| FY2032 | $19.5B | $3.5B |
| FY2033 | $19.9B | $3.8B |
| FY2034 | $20.2B | $4.0B |
| FY2035 | $20.3B | $4.2B |
| Total | $189B | $35B |

The total fell by $153B, or 81%.

**What this does not show.**
- **Not the law's effect alone.** A change between two baselines also carries every economic and technical revision CBO made in the thirteen months between them. The repository does not separate them.
- **Too early to be the Grad PLUS change.** The FY2026 figure already shows most of the fall (table), but the end of Grad PLUS applies to periods from July 1, 2026, late in FY2026. So the drop cannot be read as that provision's effect.
- **Where the borrowing goes is unknown.** Neither the CBO repository nor this proxy says how much graduate borrowing moves to private lenders. ED's final rule estimates the fall in federal disbursements (`sources.md`) and is silent on where the borrowing goes.
- **Not a loss.** The B3 loss engine is not run for this scenario, so no public share of losses changes. Whether and how this proxy should feed the engine is open (proposed card to Eleonora, `METHOD.md` 3b).
- **Both baselines are forecasts.**
- **One account only.** Related accounts in the same files are left out: Student aid administration, the TEACH Grant program account, the Federal family education loan liquidating account and the Federal student loan reserve fund.

### Volume side: ED's estimate of federal lending (docket 56 b4-student-proxy-map (b))

> **Claude draft.** Eleonora chose (2026-11-11) to add the Education Department's loan-volume estimate beside the CBO proxy, after a source check, with no change to the loss engine until she reviews it. Method: `METHOD.md` section 3c. Source, hash and quotes: [`sources.md`](sources.md).

ED's final rule (91 FR 23768, Regulatory Impact Analysis, Table 3.1) estimates federal student-loan disbursements over 2026–2035 "Pre" and "Post" the Working Families Tax Cuts Act (P.L. 119-21), as ED labels its columns. The table's source line names ED's "Student Loan Model volume assumption for PB2026" and its cost estimates for the Act; the rule's text credits the fall to "the final regulations". This is an **ED projection of federal lending**, as printed:

| Loan type | ED "Pre" | ED "Post" |
|---|---|---|
| Undergraduate | $355.8B | $352.1B |
| Graduate Stafford and Graduate PLUS | $436.4B | $265.5B |
| Parent PLUS | $154.1B | $104.9B |
| Non-consolidated total | $946.4B | $722.5B |
| Consolidation (not in the total; see below) | $454.6B | $338.7B |

Non-consolidated disbursements fall by $223.9B, or 24%, almost all of it in graduate loans ($170.9B) and Parent PLUS loans ($49.3B).

**How to read it beside the CBO proxy.**
- **Different quantities.** CBO's figure above is the projected outlays of a program account (what it pays for the loans' cost), compared across two baselines. ED's is projected loan volume from its own model. They are shown side by side, and no ratio between them is computed.
- **Federal lending only.** ED estimates how much less the government lends. Neither source says how much of that moves to private lenders, so the private side of the scenario is still unestimated.
- **No loss, no share.** Neither figure enters the B3 loss engine (her ruling), so no public share of losses changes.
- **Years: probably loan cohorts.** Table 3.1 says only "2026–2035". The same RIA states its budget estimates by loan cohort, and "A cohort reflects all loans originated in a given fiscal year", so these are probably cohort years. CBO's figures are outlays by fiscal year, which time the same loans differently.
- **Consolidation is a different flow.** Consolidation refinances existing loans and lends nothing new. ED keeps it out of its difference, and its Table 3.3 splits it into consolidation from default and not from default. Its fall is shown for completeness and not interpreted here.

## Reproduce

```bash
uv run --project pipeline python research/b3_scenarios/engine.py        # exposures (Z.1 2026-09-11)
uv run --project pipeline python research/b4_policy_scenarios/b4.py
uv run --project pipeline python research/b4_policy_scenarios/cbo_extract.py      # CBO repo at commit 284a956 (github.com)
uv run --project pipeline python research/b4_policy_scenarios/student_proxy.py
uv run --project pipeline python research/b4_policy_scenarios/ed_volume.py        # ED rule Table 3.1 (fixture: verbatim text layer)
uv run --project pipeline python research/b4_policy_scenarios/make_readme_and_rows.py
```
